correctness.rationale: A complete balance-path argument proves disjointness of maximal Dyck ends for each non-Dyck word, uniquely identifies a nonremovable core, and establishes an actual game-isomorphism with two Nim heaps; fully Dyck words are a one-heap case. Primitive Dyck decomposition gives p=z^2/(1-p); the all-word decomposition yields the core generating function; finite xor blocks give every stratum. Coefficient transfer at z=+1/2 yields the limiting geometric XOR law and the 4 sqrt(2)/(9 sqrt(pi n)) correction; z=-1/2 contributes lower order. Independent brute mex and series programs, replayed from the current package, checked 262143 words and coefficients through length 60. Computational evidence is supplementary to the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The problem is a canonical simultaneous two-sided extension of Dyck-word subtraction from a recent formal-language game framework. A structural invariant yields a complete all-word nimber classification, exact algebraic generating functions at every prescribed nimber, an infinite nonregular losing language, and a sharp limiting geometric-xor distribution with its 1/sqrt(n) approach to 1/3. The result is neither a finite enumeration nor a routine one-sided corollary; it resolves a natural full context-free rule family and makes a falsifiable prediction at every length.
